body:
Working with Claude, I've completed a sweep, looking at all 416 openai/math configurations (on 8199c74), and re-run the ten that fail on the current master. If we include the let fix in #71, the Nat.succ guard proposed above, and STACK_SIZE raised to 64 MiB, they all work.

All ten openai/math configurations that fail on master check, each in under a minute and under 3 GB memory. The guard is needed for ContinuumCoulombHardness, which overflows even at 256 MiB without it; the larger stack is needed for ContingencyTables, LogspaceEquality and MatchingFPRAS, whose Nat recursion goes deeper. Note that Lean Kernel Arena already builds nanoda with 256 MiB.

You can see the measurements and the analysis of the deep cases: https://github.com/nealmcb/openai-math-lean-tooling/blob/main/results/nanoda-stack-size-2026-10-25.txt and https://github.com/nealmcb/openai-math-lean-tooling/blob/main/results/nanoda-repro/three-stack-failures.md
